name: E1DA
_terms_not_concluded: No terms page found on e1dashz.wixsite.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding no prohibition. Measured 2026-11-25: terms, terms-of-use, terms-and-conditions, legal, privacy, privacy-policy, tos, copyright and disclaimer all 404 under /index/; no legal link in any navigation or footer; and a sweep of every page's text for « all rights reserved », « copyright », « reproduc », « redistribut », « terms of use » and « permission » returned nothing at all - not even a footer notice of the usual kind. What the footer does carry, on every page, is two lines: « (c) 2025 E1DA » and « (c) 2126 E1DA Future is here ;) ». robots.txt is Wix boilerplate, permissive, with no Content-Signal and no group naming any Claude or Anthropic agent.
_the_maker_runs_no_shop_host_of_its_own: Worth recording because it removes the scope question that has governed four brands this week. E1DA's BUY page sends buyers to an AliExpress store and to Discord and Twitter; there is no E1DA shop subdomain, so there is no shop-scoped terms document that might or might not reach the product pages. One host, thirteen pages, one answer. Contrast Shanling, where a store's prose forbade and the product host did not, and Hidizs and EarMen, where the store and the product pages were the same Shopify host and the clause reached everything.
_identifying_the_makers_own_host_took_me: e1da.com is a parked domain for sale, redirecting to hugedomains.com. e1da.net is an unrelated Australian IT company. e1dashop.com, e1da.shop, e1da.store, e1da.pro, e1da.ru and some twenty other candidates have no DNS. The maker's own site is a FREE Wix site at e1dashz.wixsite.com, and the identification rests on its content rather than its address: the ABOUT US page is written in the first person - « It's me, Ivan Khlyupin, Russian engineer lives in China for 14 years » - it hosts his own firmware, Windows drivers and Tweak applications, and it says of itself « even that web site is free ». Third-party reviews exist and the maker links them; nothing was taken from any of them.
_a_Wix_extraction_trap_measured: Wix splits running text across inline spans, and a first extraction pass broke words mid-word: « standard un/balanced », « The tut/orial ». Re-extracted by removing inline tags WITHOUT inserting whitespace, then verified against known words - unbalanced, 4000uF, tutorial, FW tools. Same family as pdftotext -layout dropping every « t » in another maker's manuals today: a silent mangling that leaves plausible output, which is the dangerous kind. Every figure under this brand is text, not OCR.
_what_this_maker_does_that_almost_none_o: Three things worth naming together. The DSD TRANSPORT DEPENDS ON THE FIRMWARE: « USB audio bridge CT7601 doesn't support native DSD in a sync mode, DoP64-128 only » - so the 9039S accepts native DSD256 on one firmware and DoP only on another. The FIRMWARE CHANGES MODE WITH THE RATE RECEIVED: the 9038SG3 runs one configuration for 44.1 to 192 kHz and another for 384 kHz and DSD, with the dB cost stated both ways. And the maker PUBLISHES ITS DEFAULTS, filter included - « Filter = Min phase » - which is rarer and worth more than a filter list, because it says what the device does before anyone touches it.
_two_devices_here_convert_WITHOUT_a_conv: The PowerDAC V2 is a fully digital PWM amplifier: « PowerDAC has no HPA at all. ... no analog amplification and no feedback are implemented there », built on a « TAS5558 Ti 8 channels digital PWM modulator » feeding « passive LC demodulation ». The HiFiTOY is the same idea - « Fully Digital Amplifier(FDA or Power DAC) » - and names no part at all. Both have `family` and `technology` ABSENT, because the technology enum offers delta_sigma, r2r, discrete_dsd and fpga and a switching modulator is none of them. First records in the base of devices that convert digital to analogue with no converter in them.
_read_and_NOT_recorded: The Cosmos DAC page exists and is linked, and contains NO specification text whatsoever - its whole body is a heading and a two-image gallery, so any figure on it is inside an image and none was read. The 9039S page explains why: three prototypes on dual ES9038Q2M, then a 9039Pro, then dual ES9039Q2M, and « That's why Cosmos DAC release is delayed again and instead of that I suddenly offer 9039S ». No shipping specification is published. Also checked and excluded as not converting digital to analogue: Cosmos ADC (the opposite direction), Cosmos APU and Cosmos Scaler, whose own page states « Device purpose: ultra-low THD+N variable gain buffer for Cosmos ADC » with analogue in and analogue out.
